rows.medi_said: I, I removed is إيديت?
rows.why: He knows the verb (sheet: 'i remove / take away | Ana ba2eem | أنا بقيم') but guessed a wrong past form; Amal gave إمت (2ayyamt) and بقيم and he took it ('بعيم, that's right. So إمت').

rows.medi_said: اليوم أنا إمت، uh, Instagram و لوب، uh، ألعاب، uh، من تلفوني
rows.why: Specific games he deleted from his phone need el-; Amal later (05:06) says 'إمت الـ Instagram والـ ألعاب' but that is two minutes later, so treated as let-pass.
rows.english: Today I removed Instagram and the games from my phone.

rows.medi_said: Do you guys use enough كافية? Is, uh، is this an Arabic word or no?
rows.why: He asked whether كافية is used; Amal supplied بكفي - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: Ah، بكافية، okay. Uh، كل، كل اليوم مش-- uh، ما عندي بكافية وقت.
rows.why: He means 'every day I don't have enough time'; kul + el- = the whole day, every day is كل يوم. Amal did not react.
rows.english: Every day I don't have enough time.

rows.medi_said: ما عندي بكافية وقت.
rows.why: بكافية is a blend of كافية and her just-given بكفي (not a word); Amal recast it as وقت بكفي.

rows.medi_said: ما عندي بكافية وقت.
rows.why: The 'enough' word goes after the noun (وقت بكفي); Amal's reply puts it after وقت. Same moment as the vocab row.

rows.medi_said: راح، راح أسعد. Yeah، راح يسعد. Yeah، راح يسعدني.
rows.amal_said: راح يساعد. Mhm. ... يعني لسه ما ساعد.
rows.why: Answering 'did anything change?' he meant 'it will help'; يسعد (make happy) is a different word, Amal recast to يساعد and followed with 'لسه ما ساعد', which he translated ('still doesn't help?'). Could be a vowel-length slip (F2).

rows.medi_said: بفكر إنه كل إشي بيحر-- كل إشي بيحر-- بيحرك.
rows.amal_said: بيت حرك. ... لا، بيت is you getting moved. So كل إشي gets moved.
rows.why: بيحرك = moves something; for 'everything is moving' Amal gave بيتحرك and explained the t- form is getting moved.
rows.english: I think everything is moving (so fast).

rows.medi_said: مش بارد، مش شوب، uh، بين، بينو، بينهم.
rows.why: For weather 'in between' Amal echoed بينهم then gave نص نص, which he repeated; may be her offering an alternative, so low.
rows.english: Not cold, not hot, in between.

rows.medi_said: بدك، بدك المطر؟
rows.why: He meant 'do you like the rain?' (she just said it was nice); بدك = want. She answered with بحب and he took it ('بـ-بتحب، yeah').

rows.medi_said: الفلسطينيين، uh، ناخد المطر؟ المي؟
rows.why: Subject is the Palestinians (they) but the verb is we-form ناخد with no b-; Amal only asked what he meant.

rows.medi_said: الفلسطينيين، uh، ناخد المطر؟ المي؟
rows.why: 'Take the rain' for 'collect rainwater' - Amal could not follow ('كيف يعني؟') and he switched to English; the right verb is my reading (جمع), not hers.

rows.medi_said: أنا جربت بس الـ set، uh, يخرب، uh, يخرب-- يخرب-- يخرب؟
rows.why: Telling what happened (the card set broke) needs past; he said present يخرب and asked, Amal gave past خربه; he then said خربوا 'That's right'.
rows.english: I tried, but the set broke (it).

rows.medi_said: بنت به. Uh, بنت به. Yeah, بنت, بنت به is to, to take care of something.
rows.amal_said: Actually، بنتبه is more like pay attention.
rows.right: بنتبه = pay attention (ديري بالك = take care)
rows.why: Asked for 'pay attention' vs 'take care', he gave انتبه for take care; Amal said it means pay attention and he said 'Oh, whoops'.
rows.english: Which word means take care / pay attention.

rows.medi_said: Is it لا? I don't remember this one.
rows.why: Quizzed on the preposition بنتبه takes, he guessed لـ; Amal gave على ('الاتنين بياخدوا على'). A guess with a question mark - could be read as a question.

rows.medi_said: أنا لازم أتدرب، uh, ستي ... بتدرب لا؟
rows.amal_said: وبتدرب شو، شو بتدرب بتاخد؟ ... A preposition. ... على.
rows.why: He left out the preposition after أتدرب; Amal prompted ('A preposition'), he guessed لا, and she supplied على.
rows.english: I have to practice the set.

rows.medi_said: Great. تمارنتي
rows.why: She asked for a command; he said a past-tense 'you (f) exercised' form, Amal said 'أمر' (command) and he changed to تمارني.

rows.medi_said: بيجيب اللي. ... بيجيب اللي أي. Yeah.
rows.amal_said: جبيلي إياه. Why did you put be؟
rows.why: A command has no b-; Amal gave جيبلي إياه and asked why he put the b-.

rows.medi_said: Trump hadeekna, tehekna.
rows.why: 'Fool someone' is ضحك على; he said hadeekna (made us laugh) and Amal repeated ضحك until he said tehekalayna.

rows.medi_said: harb jadeed. Jadeeda.
rows.amal_said: حرب. جدد. We didn't learn the plural for حرب. ... حروب.
rows.why: He meant 'no new wars'; Amal said they had not learned the plural and supplied حروب / جداد - a didn't-know (his jadeed->jadeeda was a self-fix).

rows.medi_said: Hadik al-dawla, uh, is, uh, biddik jibal.
rows.amal_said: الجبال. ... جبال. جبال. جبل. جبل is one.
rows.why: For 'if you like mountains' Amal recast with el- (الجبال) and he asked 'What did I say?'; her follow-up may only be the plural sound jbaal, so low.
rows.english: Travel to that country if you like mountains.

rows.medi_said: Surprise. It's, uh, I don't know how to say surprise.
rows.why: He said he did not know 'surprise'; Amal supplied مفاجأة.
rows.english: Keep quiet about the party because it's a surprise.

rows.medi_said: [his lines 44:57-47:22 are missing from the transcript]
rows.amal_said: Baraw-barawih. What do you think? It's a double something, but not R. ... it's already indicated that's like rawahi.
rows.why: Amal coached the command 'go home' (double w, روحي); his attempts were not transcribed, so the wrong form is unknown.

rows.medi_said: [his line missing from the transcript]
rows.amal_said: If I want to say the beit, I would have to say to the home. So what's the to part? Ala el beit. So rawahi ala el beit badri.
rows.why: Amal said 'to the home' needs على and gave the full sentence; his own line was not transcribed.

rows.medi_said: [his line missing from the transcript]
rows.amal_said: it's a wrong form. Let's go back home. La la. Right verb, but wrong command form. ... We said it's a double W. So rawahi.
rows.wrong: (wrong command form of بروح, not transcribed)
rows.why: Amal said 'Right verb, but wrong command form' and gave rawahi; his sentence is missing from the transcript.
rows.english: Let's go back home / go home.

rows.medi_said: Because you forgot your keys, so ashan nisti ma-- uh... But what is it for you feminine? Is it nisti?
rows.amal_said: Mm. So you forgot. It's one of the irregulars. ... Nseeti because, because you is nseed.
rows.why: Past 'you (f) forgot' is irregular نسيتي; he used nisti in his sentence and Amal gave nseeti, which he repeated.

rows.medi_said: أنا برجع، uh, [speaking foreign language] right?
rows.why: Amal supplied من الgym and he said 'Oh, you said من؟ أنا برجع من الجيم'; his words were partly not transcribed.
rows.english: I come back from the gym.

rows.medi_said: حوالي، uh, تيس-- ... Would I say تيس على تيس؟
rows.why: Clock time needs el- (على التسع); he said تيس bare and Amal recast twice, he repeated على التيس.

rows.medi_said: [speaking foreign language] على. And that one is logical.
rows.why: 'Keep quiet about' is اسكت عن; he gave على and Amal said عن.

rows.medi_said: So a la, a la. A la i?
rows.why: Command of بقلق needs the i- prefix (اقلقي); he tried a-la-i and Amal gave اقلقي, he repeated 'it la i'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, khafi, khafi.
rows.why: For 'scare me' he used khafi (get scared); Amal said 'No' and he moved to the doubled-middle خوفني.

rows.medi_said: khawaf, khawafni.
rows.amal_said: بلاش. خوفني، yes. مش إي. Did you put an إي؟
rows.why: A doubled-middle verb's command takes no i-; Amal said 'مش إي' and he admitted 'I did' put one, then said khawafni.
